source: California Regional Water Quality Control Board, Central Valley Region (R5) — Nonpoint Source Unit
obtained: 2026-07 (Public Records Act response, analyst Courtney Kasich)
area: Dixie Fire burn scar, Greenville watershed, Plumas County
finding: The Dixie Fire/Greenville stations are monitored for post-fire recovery, not for the herbicides applied in the watershed; no herbicide analyte appears in their sampling panel. County-wide, CEDEN Plumas data 2018-2026 contain one herbicide sampling event: Benner Creek above Lake Almanor, 2022-10-03, collected by Sierra Pacific Industries Research. Glyphosate, imazapyr and aminopyralid not detected; hexazinone trace 0.0013 ug/L (detected, below reporting limit 0.005 ug/L); QA-flagged: the lab batch's spike-recovery checks (matrix spike/duplicate and lab control sample, CEDEN batch comment "QAO: MS/MSD and LCS %R out") were out of range, so this trace is low-confidence. Triclopyr and 2,4-D never tested.

ceden_herbicide_sampling.name: Benner Creek about 2.5 km above Lake Almanor

hexazinone.qa_flag: QA-flagged: the lab batch's spike-recovery checks (matrix spike/duplicate and lab control sample, CEDEN batch comment "QAO: MS/MSD and LCS %R out") were out of range, so this trace is low-confidence

stations.location: Setzer Camp Creek / Greenville-Wolf Creek Roads

notified_but_not_tested: USFS formally notifies the Water Board of herbicide operations (e.g. Wildcat project: aminopyralid <7 oz/acre + Competitor surfactant, backpack/hand spray, June-Sept, per a 2023 notice) and herbicide/reforestation work is tracked for BMP compliance — but the water is not screened for these compounds.
